video:video.video:title: Electric Two-Wheeler Makers in India Face Margin Squeeze as AI Infrastructure Boom Drives Up Chip Co
video:video.video:description: India's electric two-wheeler manufacturers are facing significant margin pressure and potential retail price increases as raw material costs surge and global AI infrastructure demand intensifies competition for lithium-ion cells and memory chips. The AI data centre boom is creating upstream supply chain pressure that is now directly affecting the cost of affordable EVs for Indian commuters. Manufacturers warn that price hikes may be unavoidable unless government intervention stabilises input costs, with implications for India's EV adoption targets and the tens of millions of households considering a switch from petrol bikes.

video:video.video:title: HrdWyr Raises $13M Series A From Ideaspring Capital to Develop Fabless Semiconductor Chips in India
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based fabless semiconductor startup HrdWyr has raised $13 million in a Series A round led by Ideaspring Capital to fund product development and market expansion. The company designs chips without owning its own manufacturing facilities, a model that allows Indian startups to compete in semiconductor design while the country builds out its fabrication ecosystem. The funding comes as India pushes to build domestic chip design capacity alongside its semiconductor manufacturing ambitions, with HrdWyr representing an emerging cohort of deep-tech startups that could reduce India's dependence on foreign chip architectures.

video:video.video:title: Tamil Nadu Police Used IT Rules to Ask X to Block 18 URLs Belonging to Ruling Party's Critics
video:video.video:description: Tamil Nadu Police invoked Section 79(3)(b) of India's IT Act to request that X (formerly Twitter) block 18 URLs, which allegedly belong to DMK supporters who shared commentary criticising the Tamil Viduthalai Kazhagam party and the Chief Minister's office. The requests represent a pattern of state-level police agencies using federal IT law powers to suppress political speech online, bypassing judicial oversight. The incident adds to a growing record of India's content takedown infrastructure being used against domestic political dissent rather than solely for national security or harm-prevention purposes.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC Restores Blocked YouTube Channel 4PM, Orders Transparency in Government Blocking Process
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court has ordered the temporary restoration of the YouTube channel 4PM, which was blocked by the Union government citing national security concerns, while simultaneously directing a fresh hearing before the Inter-Departmental Committee and demanding greater transparency in the blocking process. The court's order signals judicial discomfort with opaque executive use of content blocking powers under India's IT Rules, especially as AI-generated content and algorithmic flagging make the volume of takedown requests harder to contest. The ruling has direct implications for how digital platforms and independent media creators in India navigate government-initiated content removal.

video:video.video:title: ekincare Builds CIBIL-Style Health Score for Corporate India After a Decade of Structured Health Dat
video:video.video:description: Hyderabad-based healthtech startup ekincare has spent ten years aggregating structured employee health data and is now positioning that dataset as the foundation for a CIBIL-equivalent health score for corporate India. The platform is already embedded in corporate healthcare programmes and uses longitudinal data to predict health risks, guide interventions and inform insurance decisions. The model goes beyond employee wellness apps by creating a persistent, AI-readable health profile that could influence how Indian employers and insurers assess individual risk over time.

video:video.video:title: Agentic AI Moves From Lab to Real-World Deployment Across Indian Startups, Edtech and Healthcare
video:video.video:description: A new analysis finds that agentic AI — systems capable of taking multi-step actions autonomously without human prompting — is now moving from experimentation into active deployment across Indian startups, edtech platforms and healthcare providers. Organisations pulling ahead are those that have invested in the underlying AI architecture, not just model selection, suggesting that implementation quality is becoming a competitive differentiator. For Indian businesses in education and health sectors that serve hundreds of millions of users, the shift to agentic AI represents a meaningful change in how services are delivered, personalised and scaled.

video:video.video:title: PB Fintech Says AI Will Transform Insurance Claims Processing as Paisabazaar Enters Debt Broking
video:video.video:description: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, announced in its Q4 FY26 results that artificial intelligence will fundamentally transform how insurance claims are processed for Indian consumers, while also revealing that Paisabazaar has entered the debt broking segment. The company launched expanded insurance coverage categories including gym memberships, OPD consultations and maternity, areas where AI-driven assessment could streamline previously manual approval processes. The dual announcement signals PB Fintech's strategy to use AI not only for customer acquisition but for the full claims lifecycle, which directly affects how quickly and accurately Indian policyholders receive payouts.

video:video.video:title: India Notifies Social Security Rules 2026: Swiggy, Zomato and Ola Must Register Gig Workers in Real
video:video.video:description: India has formally notified the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, requiring gig economy platforms including Swiggy, Zomato and Ola to register gig workers with the government in real time and meet ongoing compliance obligations. The rules mandate that platforms report worker data continuously rather than periodically, marking a significant expansion of the state's oversight of algorithmically managed workforces. This is the first time India's gig economy has faced live, platform-level statutory reporting requirements, with direct implications for how AI-driven dispatch and rating systems interact with labour law.

video:video.video:title: Supreme Court Set to Hear Petitions Challenging India's First Digital Privacy Law This Month
video:video.video:description: India's Supreme Court is expected to hear petitions this month challenging key sections of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the country's first dedicated privacy law. Petitioners including the Reporters' Collective, the Editors Guild of India, and transparency activist Venkatesh Nayak argue that provisions amending the Right to Information Act could enable blanket denial of information requests involving personal data. The outcome could fundamentally reshape how AI systems and digital platforms handle Indian citizens' data and respond to public accountability requests.

video:video.video:title: Indian Companies Rush to Buy Cyber Insurance as AI Agent Risks and Rogue Chatbots Create New Liabili
video:video.video:description: Indian companies are increasingly purchasing cyber insurance policies to protect against AI-specific risks, including AI agents acting autonomously in harmful ways and chatbots providing incorrect or dangerous information. Insurers are redesigning their underwriting models to assess AI exposure, marking a significant shift in how corporate India manages technological liability. The global AI insurance market is projected for substantial growth, and India's uptake signals that boardrooms are treating AI risk as a mainstream financial concern rather than a fringe scenario.

video:video.video:title: Can Orbital Data Centres Solve AI's Soaring Energy Demand? ISRO and Google's Suncatcher Explore Spac
video:video.video:description: As AI models consume ever-greater quantities of energy, Google's Project Suncatcher is experimenting with placing data centres in low-earth orbit to harness continuous solar energy, bypassing the land and grid constraints that limit ground-based facilities. ISRO is also reportedly studying the feasibility of space-based data centre technology as part of India's expanding space economy ambitions. The concept, while still experimental, is gaining traction globally as the energy cost of training and running large AI models becomes a critical bottleneck for the industry.

video:video.video:title: IT Body NITES Urges India's Labour Ministry to Mandate Work From Home for IT Workers Amid Oil Price
video:video.video:description: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has formally urged India's Ministry of Labour and Employment to issue an advisory mandating work-from-home arrangements for IT workers wherever operationally feasible, citing rising fuel costs and the broader economic burden on tech employees commuting to offices. The request comes as oil prices surge amid regional geopolitical tensions, placing renewed pressure on Indian IT workers' disposable income. NITES argues that India's IT sector has already demonstrated its ability to operate effectively remotely and that a formal advisory would provide legal backing for employees to request flexible arrangements.

video:video.video:title: HP Launches First Tablet and New AI PC Range in India, Including AMD-Powered EliteBoard G1a
video:video.video:description: HP has launched its first tablet in India alongside a new range of AI-enabled PCs, including the HP EliteBoard G1a AI keyboard PC powered by AMD processors delivering up to 50 TOPS of neural processing unit performance. The AI PC range is designed to handle on-device AI tasks such as real-time transcription, image generation, and intelligent search without requiring cloud connectivity. The launch marks HP's entry into India's tablet market and signals the commercial arrival of dedicated AI computing hardware for mainstream Indian consumers and enterprises.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC to Rule on Whether Indian Government Bypassed Tender Process for National Emergency Alert S
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court is set to rule on whether the Indian government bypassed a competitive tender process when awarding the contract for India's national emergency alert system to state-run CDOT, following a petition filed by Germany-based Utimaco. The case raises fundamental questions about procurement transparency and whether a monopoly arrangement for critical public safety infrastructure is legally defensible. An urgent hearing has been triggered, indicating the court views the matter as time-sensitive given the system's role in national emergency communications.

video:video.video:title: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Pledges to Make Uttar Pradesh India's Deep Tech Capital
video:video.video:description: On National Technology Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath committed to transforming UP into India's Deep Tech Capital, citing the state's rapid emergence as a hub for IT parks, manufacturing, and startups. The announcement reflects a concerted state-level push to attract AI and semiconductor investment to India's most populous state, which is already home to the HCL-Foxconn semiconductor joint venture in Jewar. The declaration adds political weight to UP's ambition to rival Bengaluru and Hyderabad as a technology destination.

video:video.video:title: Karnataka Plans AI and Deeptech Innovation Centres in Tier-II and Tier-III Cities Beyond Bengaluru
video:video.video:description: Karnataka's State Planning and Policy Commission has proposed a roadmap to decentralise the state's technology ecosystem by establishing Karnataka Innovation Orchestration Centers in tier-II and tier-III cities, moving beyond Bengaluru's dominant tech corridor. The plan targets deeptech incubation, applied AI research, and R&D activity in smaller urban centres as part of a strategy to make Karnataka a global model for technology-driven inclusive development. The initiative follows growing concern that Bengaluru's saturation is limiting India's broader tech expansion.

video:video.video:title: AI-Enabled Oversight Layer Proposed for Continuous Electoral Roll Monitoring in India
video:video.video:description: Following structural weaknesses exposed during the Special Intensive Revision 2.0 process, experts have proposed integrating an AI-enabled oversight layer with the Election Commission's ECINet platform to continuously monitor electoral roll accuracy in real time. The system would detect anomalies, flag discriminatory voter deletion patterns, and strengthen transparency and accountability in India's electoral infrastructure. The proposal represents a significant shift from periodic manual audits to AI-driven continuous surveillance of one of democracy's most critical databases.

video:video.video:title: India Pushes for Sovereign Control Over Advanced AI Cybersecurity Systems Amid Anthropic Concerns
video:video.video:description: India is actively seeking sovereign control over advanced AI systems used in cybersecurity after concerns emerged regarding Anthropic's Claude Mythos model and its capacity to detect and potentially exploit software vulnerabilities in critical national infrastructure sectors. The push reflects growing government anxiety that dependence on foreign AI models for security functions poses an unacceptable national risk. MeitY is reported to be in direct discussions to secure guaranteed access and oversight terms before such models are deployed in sensitive Indian systems.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC Passes Interim Order Protecting Shark Tank's Aman Gupta's Personality Rights Against Deepfa
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court issued an interim order protecting the personality rights of entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge Aman Gupta after AI-generated deepfake content misrepresenting him was found circulating online. The order goes beyond merely targeting fake AI videos and could establish broader legal precedent for how personality rights are enforced against AI misuse in India. Legal observers note this ruling may reshape platform liability and enforcement obligations for AI-generated impersonation content nationally.

video:video.video:title: India's AI Job Market Growing 15–20% Annually, Says Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
video:video.video:description: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw confirmed that AI-related job openings in India's IT sector are growing at 15–20% annually, making it one of the fastest-expanding employment categories in the country. The minister attributed the growth partly to significant data centre investments driven by favourable tax incentives and expanding digital infrastructure including new subsea cable projects. The statement was made in the context of India's broader push to position itself as a global AI hub.

video:video.video:title: India's IT Rules and Online Speech: Expert Event Report Flags Censorship and Platform Compliance Ris
video:video.video:description: Medianama has published an event report from its April 2026 roundtable on India's amended IT Rules, where legal experts, civil society representatives, and platform compliance teams raised concerns about the scope of content takedown powers, free speech implications, and the burden placed on intermediaries. The report documents specific provisions in the March 2026 IT Rules amendments that experts argue could enable executive overreach in regulating online speech without adequate judicial oversight. The discussion included perspectives on how platform compliance frameworks may structurally disadvantage smaller Indian publishers and independent journalists.

video:video.video:title: Kerala Citizen Builds Crowd-Sourced Website to Track Power Cuts Across All 14 Districts in Real Time
video:video.video:description: Alkesh Das, frustrated by frequent and unannounced power cuts, built a crowd-sourced platform that now allows thousands of Kerala residents to report and track electricity outages across all 14 districts of the state in real time. The tool aggregates citizen-submitted data to create a live map of power disruptions, giving households and small businesses advance notice and helping them plan around blackouts. The platform has grown organically with no institutional backing, driven entirely by community participation.

video:video.video:title: India's First Orbital Data Centre Satellite: What the Pixxel-Sarvam AI Partnership Actually Involves
video:video.video:description: The Hindu has published an explainer on India's first orbital data centre satellite, a planned mission by Pixxel and Sarvam AI that would place AI compute infrastructure in low-earth orbit, enabling satellite-based AI data processing far from terrestrial energy and cooling constraints. The piece outlines what an orbital data centre is, why global firms are racing to develop the concept, and what the specific Pixxel-Sarvam collaboration entails for India's space and AI ambitions. The mission is scheduled for 2026 and represents a convergence of India's private space sector and its generative AI ecosystem.

video:video.video:title: Paytm Rules Out NBFC Licence Plans, Stays Silent on Wallet Revival as It Pivots to Agentic AI Strate
video:video.video:description: Paytm has publicly ruled out applying for a Non-Banking Financial Company licence, distancing itself from rivals pushing deeper into lending, while remaining silent on whether it will seek revival of its payments wallet licence following the RBI's crackdown on its payments bank arm. The company's Q4 FY26 earnings call instead indicated a strategic pivot toward agentic AI capabilities and wealthtech services as its primary growth engines. This positions Paytm as an AI-first fintech platform rather than a traditional financial services provider.

video:video.video:title: Kissht Fintech Makes Strong Stock Market Debut With Shares Up 22% After Rs 926 Crore IPO
video:video.video:description: Digital lending platform Kissht made a strong debut on Indian stock markets with its shares rising 22% on listing day, following a Rs 926 crore IPO comprising both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale. The listing reflects continued investor confidence in India's digital lending sector despite regulatory scrutiny around consumer credit practices. Kissht primarily targets underserved borrowers seeking small-ticket consumer loans, operating in a segment that remains largely untouched by traditional banks.

video:video.video:title: Swiggy and Magicpin Report Improving Delivery Times as Gig Workers Return to Indian Cities After Ele
video:video.video:description: Food delivery platforms Swiggy and Magicpin have reported improving delivery times as gig workers return to urban centres following state elections and the peak harvest season, both of which had drawn large numbers of delivery partners back to rural areas. The temporary workforce contraction had stretched delivery windows and reduced platform reliability for urban consumers. Both companies expect full normalisation of delivery operations within days as rider availability recovers.

video:video.video:title: Meesho Posts Rs 166 Crore Loss in Q4 FY26 Despite 47% Revenue Jump and 264 Million Active Users
video:video.video:description: Meesho reported a 47% year-on-year revenue increase in Q4 FY26, supported by 264 million annual transacting users and a 45% rise in order volumes, even as average order values dipped slightly. Despite strong top-line growth, the company remained loss-making with a Rs 166 crore deficit for the quarter, reflecting continued investment in logistics and platform expansion. Meesho's scale makes it one of the largest e-commerce platforms serving price-sensitive consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 Indian cities.

video:video.video:title: Anthropic's Mythos AI Model Is a Double-Edged Sword — It Finds and Can Exploit Cyber Vulnerabilities
video:video.video:description: The Hindu's analysis of Anthropic's Mythos AI model highlights its dual-use nature: it can identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities that human analysts miss, but it can equally generate working exploits — potentially placing advanced cyberattack capabilities in the hands of non-experts. This capability is particularly alarming for India's critical infrastructure sectors, including banking, telecommunications, and government systems, which have historically operated with slower patch cycles. The piece contextualises Mythos within India's ongoing negotiations with Anthropic and CERT-In's preparedness assessments.

video:video.video:title: US Official Warns India to Avoid AI Dependencies on Adversarial Nations as US-India Tech Partnership
video:video.video:description: A senior US official has urged India to avoid building strategic dependencies on adversarial nations in AI development, framing openness and trusted partnerships as essential to unlocking AI's economic potential. The statement signals a deepening US-India alignment on AI supply chain security, with both governments emphasising regional access to world-class technology. The remarks come amid India's rapid GPU capacity expansion and growing scrutiny of Chinese AI hardware and software inputs.

video:video.video:title: IndiaAI Mission Startups Hit by Paperwork Delays — Funding and IP Concerns Stall Momentum
video:video.video:description: Startups selected under India's IndiaAI Mission are facing delays in formal agreement signings, with pending MoUs holding up non-compute support and raising intellectual property ownership concerns among founders. While compute access has been provisioned, operational hurdles are pushing timelines and dampening the program's early momentum. The government is reportedly exploring advance payment mechanisms to address cash-flow pressures on participating startups.

video:video.video:title: Fi Money Shuts Consumer Banking, Pivots to AI and Enterprise Tech After Co-Founder Gwalani Exits
video:video.video:description: Fi Money co-founder Sumit Gwalani has stepped down after six years, following the March 2026 shutdown of the neobank's consumer banking service and a broader strategic pivot toward AI and enterprise technology. The departure underscores the mounting pressures facing India's neobanking sector, where regulatory constraints on banking partnerships have made pure-play consumer neobanking increasingly difficult to sustain. The company's shift toward enterprise AI signals a growing trend of Indian fintech startups repositioning away from consumer finance toward B2B AI services.

video:video.video:title: OpenAI Adds Trusted Contact Safety Feature to ChatGPT to Flag Self-Harm Conversations in Real Time
video:video.video:description: OpenAI has rolled out a Trusted Contact feature in ChatGPT that allows users to designate a contact person who will be notified by email or SMS if the AI detects self-harm conversations, with the contact informed of their role at the point of being added. The feature is directly relevant to India where ChatGPT usage is growing rapidly and mental health support infrastructure remains uneven. It represents one of the most concrete AI safety guardrails yet built into a major consumer AI platform for vulnerable users.

video:video.video:title: Adobe Opens New Noida Office With AI Innovation Focus as India Deepens Its Role in Global R&D
video:video.video:description: Adobe has expanded its India footprint with a new office in Noida, explicitly positioned as a centre for advancing AI-driven innovation and marking what the company calls an important milestone in driving global product development from India. The opening reflects a broader trend of multinational technology firms deepening their India R&D and AI engineering presence as Indian talent pools grow. Adobe has significant India operations and the new facility is expected to support work on AI-powered creative and document tools.

video:video.video:title: IIT Madras Opens First US Centre in Silicon Valley to Bridge Indian Deeptech Research and Global Mar
video:video.video:description: IIT Madras has established its first overseas centre in Silicon Valley, aimed at serving as a launchpad for Indian deeptech startups through research commercialisation and connections with the US tech ecosystem. The centre is intended to help Indian founders and researchers translate laboratory innovations into globally competitive products. This move comes as India accelerates efforts to build a deeptech pipeline that can compete internationally in AI, semiconductors, and advanced engineering.

video:video.video:title: Zepto Receives SEBI Approval for $1 Billion IPO, Clearing Path to Public Markets
video:video.video:description: Quick commerce startup Zepto has received SEBI's observations on its draft red herring prospectus, effectively securing regulatory clearance to proceed with its $1 billion initial public offering. SEBI issued the observations between May 4 and 8 as part of a batch covering six companies, marking a significant milestone for one of India's fastest-growing consumer tech startups. The IPO will be among the largest in India's new-age tech sector and reflects growing investor confidence in quick commerce as a durable business model.

video:video.video:title: Swiggy Q4 Revenue Surges 45% to Rs 6,383 Crore as Net Loss Narrows to Rs 800 Crore
video:video.video:description: Swiggy reported a 45% year-on-year revenue surge to Rs 6,383 crore in Q4 FY26, with its net loss narrowing significantly to Rs 800 crore as both its food delivery and Instamart quick commerce arms gained traction. The company is targeting a Rs 1 lakh crore net order value for Instamart, indicating aggressive long-term ambitions in the quick commerce segment. CEO Sriharsha Majety cautioned that strategic clarity — not unchecked spending — will determine which platforms survive the current quick commerce boom.

video:video.video:title: DesignX Builds Factory OS and Vish.ai to Turn Industrial Data Into Real-Time Decisions for 30+ Enter
video:video.video:description: Indian startup DesignX has developed Df-OS, a factory operating system, and Vish.ai, an AI decision layer, that convert raw factory data into actionable operational decisions in real time. The platform is already deployed across more than 30 enterprises including Unilever, Hero, and ITC, positioning DesignX as a meaningful player in India's industrial AI space. The solution targets manufacturing efficiency bottlenecks by replacing manual data interpretation with autonomous AI-driven recommendations.

video:video.video:title: GoKwik Launches AI-Powered Kwik Ship to Cut Failed E-Commerce Deliveries by 20% Across India
video:video.video:description: GoKwik has launched Kwik Ship, an AI-powered logistics platform designed to reduce failed deliveries by up to 20% for Indian e-commerce brands. The system uses AI-powered calls and automated WhatsApp notifications to keep customers informed and provides more accurate delivery time estimates at checkout. The platform directly addresses one of Indian e-commerce's most persistent pain points — high return-to-origin rates caused by failed deliveries.

video:video.video:title: Paytm Bets on Agentic AI and Wealthtech as Core Growth Pillars After RBI Payments Bank Shutdown
video:video.video:description: In its Q4 FY26 earnings call, Paytm revealed a strategic pivot toward agentic AI and wealthtech services as the primary drivers of its next growth phase, following the RBI-mandated shutdown of its payments bank arm. The company has ruled out applying for an NBFC licence, instead focusing on AI-powered financial tools and investment products for its existing user base. The shift represents a significant repositioning of one of India's largest fintech platforms toward autonomous AI-driven financial services.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC Orders Removal of Deepfake Videos Falsely Showing MP Shashi Tharoor Praising Pakistan
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court announced it would issue blocking orders against AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting Congress MP Shashi Tharoor praising Pakistan, after he filed a petition over the misuse of his identity. The case marks one of the most prominent Indian legal interventions involving political deepfakes during an active security-sensitive period. The ruling signals growing judicial willingness to act swiftly against AI-generated political disinformation in India.

video:video.video:title: Proshort AI Sales Coaching Platform Crosses $1M ARR Within a Year of Launch
video:video.video:description: Indian AI startup Proshort, founded by Gaurav Mishra, has reached $1 million in annual recurring revenue within its first year by offering real-time AI sales coaching that delivers live insights to sales professionals during customer interactions. The platform targets India's large and growing sales workforce, providing on-the-job AI assistance without requiring formal training programmes. Crossing $1M ARR in year one positions Proshort among the faster-growing B2B AI SaaS companies to emerge from India in 2025–26.

video:video.video:title: Fi Money Shuts Consumer Banking, Pivots to AI and Enterprise Tech After Co-Founder Gwalani Exits
video:video.video:description: Fi Money co-founder Sumit Gwalani has stepped down after six years, following the March 2026 shutdown of the neobank's consumer banking service and a broader strategic pivot toward AI and enterprise technology. The departure underscores the mounting pressures facing India's neobanking sector, where regulatory constraints on banking partnerships have made pure-play consumer neobanking increasingly difficult to sustain. The company's shift toward enterprise AI signals a growing trend of Indian fintech startups repositioning away from consumer finance toward B2B AI services.

video:video.video:title: Ecofy Raises $15M From Mirova to Expand Green Financing Portfolio Across India's Energy Transition
video:video.video:description: Indian green fintech startup Ecofy has raised $15 million from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers, to expand its portfolio of financing products for India's energy transition. The investment marks Mirova's fourth deal in India under its emerging markets climate mandate, underlining growing international confidence in Indian green finance infrastructure. Ecofy targets underserved segments of India's clean energy economy, including rooftop solar and energy-efficient consumer products, with AI-assisted credit underwriting.

video:video.video:title: Karnataka Plans Dedicated SpaceTech Testing Facilities and Manufacturing Parks Under DeepTech Decade
video:video.video:description: Karnataka has announced plans to expand its role in India's commercial space economy through a DeepTech Decade vision that includes common testing facilities and dedicated manufacturing parks for space startups and MSMEs. The initiative targets reducing the infrastructure barrier that prevents smaller players from accessing space-grade testing environments. Bengaluru, already home to ISRO and dozens of spacetech startups, is positioned as the state's anchor hub for this push.

video:video.video:title: India and Japan Sign Quantum Technology and Health Research Cooperation Agreements
video:video.video:description: India and Japan have formalised bilateral agreements to collaborate on quantum science and medical device research, aiming to jointly advance science, technology, and innovation partnerships. The deals are intended to foster joint R&D projects and strengthen academic and industrial ties between the two nations. The quantum technology agreement is particularly significant as India races to build domestic capabilities in post-classical computing alongside its AI infrastructure push.

video:video.video:title: Zee Sues Nykaa in Delhi HC Over Copyrighted Songs Used in Instagram Reels Ads Without Permission
video:video.video:description: Zee Entertainment has filed a lawsuit against beauty e-commerce platform Nykaa in the Delhi High Court, alleging that Nykaa used Zee's copyrighted songs in Instagram Reels advertising campaigns without obtaining licences or paying royalties, and seeking Rs 2 crore in damages. The case could set a landmark precedent for how Indian brands are required to clear music rights before using short-form video content for commercial promotion on social media platforms. Legal experts say the outcome may reshape compliance practices across India's digital advertising industry.

video:video.video:title: India's PoS Terminal Shortage Deepens as China Import Disruptions Push Device Prices Up 15–20%
video:video.video:description: India's digital payments industry is grappling with a shortage of new point-of-sale terminals caused by disruptions to imports from China and the West Asia conflict, pushing device prices up by 15–20%. Payments companies are being forced to extend the lifecycles of existing terminals and manage their installed base more carefully. The squeeze threatens the expansion of card and UPI acceptance infrastructure at India's retail merchants.

video:video.video:title: Adobe Opens New Noida Office With AI Innovation Focus as India Deepens Its Role in Global R&D
video:video.video:description: Adobe has expanded its India footprint with a new office in Noida, explicitly positioned as a centre for advancing AI-driven innovation and marking what the company calls an important milestone in driving global product development from India. The opening reflects a broader trend of multinational technology firms deepening their India R&D and AI engineering presence as Indian talent pools grow. Adobe has significant India operations and the new facility is expected to support work on AI-powered creative and document tools.

video:video.video:title: Hexaware Q1 CY26 Net Profit Rises 7.5% to Rs 352 Crore as European and Banking Segments Drive Growth
video:video.video:description: Hexaware Technologies posted a 7.5% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 351.6 crore in Q1 CY26, beating analyst expectations, with revenue growing 12.6% to Rs 3,613 crore. Growth was led by strong performance in Europe and the banking and financial services vertical. The company maintained its full-year revenue growth guidance of 7.6%, suggesting steady demand for its AI-augmented IT services.

video:video.video:title: BigEndian Semiconductors Raises $6M Led by IAN Alpha Fund to Commercialise Its First System-on-Chip
video:video.video:description: Indian semiconductor startup BigEndian Semiconductors has secured $6 million in funding led by IAN Alpha Fund, with the capital earmarked to commercialise its first system-on-chip product, expand its product engineering team, and deepen partnerships with foundries, IP ecosystems, and OEMs. The raise is notable in the context of India's push to build a domestic semiconductor industry, as BigEndian represents a rare homegrown chip design company reaching commercial readiness. The investment also reflects growing domestic venture confidence in India's semiconductor ambitions following recent government fab approvals.

video:video.video:title: Zepto Receives SEBI Approval for $1 Billion IPO, Clearing Path to Public Markets
video:video.video:description: Quick commerce startup Zepto has received SEBI's observations on its draft red herring prospectus, effectively securing regulatory clearance to proceed with its $1 billion initial public offering. SEBI issued the observations between May 4 and 8 as part of a batch covering six companies, marking a significant milestone for one of India's fastest-growing consumer tech startups. The IPO will be among the largest in India's new-age tech sector and reflects growing investor confidence in quick commerce as a durable business model.

video:video.video:title: Karnataka's ELEVATE NxT Deep-Tech Programme Draws 983 Applications, Nearly 23% From Outside State
video:video.video:description: Karnataka's government-backed deep-tech startup programme ELEVATE NxT has received 983 applications, with 213 — nearly 23% — coming from startups outside the state, indicating national appetite for structured deep-tech support. The programme is designed to accelerate startups working on frontier technologies including AI, semiconductors, and advanced engineering. The strong cross-state response signals that India's deep-tech startup ecosystem is maturing beyond Bengaluru's traditional boundaries.

video:video.video:title: Freo Acquires Credit Marketplace IndiaLends to Serve Over 50 Million Users via Combined Platform
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based digital banking platform Freo has acquired IndiaLends, a credit marketplace, in a move that will give the combined entity access to more than 50 million users. IndiaLends will continue to operate as a separate brand while leveraging Freo's digital banking infrastructure. The acquisition consolidates two platforms targeting overlapping segments of India's underserved credit market.

video:video.video:title: Swiggy Q4 Revenue Surges 45% to Rs 6,383 Crore as Net Loss Narrows to Rs 800 Crore
video:video.video:description: Swiggy reported a 45% year-on-year revenue surge to Rs 6,383 crore in Q4 FY26, with its net loss narrowing significantly to Rs 800 crore as both its food delivery and Instamart quick commerce arms gained traction. The company is targeting a Rs 1 lakh crore net order value for Instamart, indicating aggressive long-term ambitions in the quick commerce segment. CEO Sriharsha Majety cautioned that strategic clarity — not unchecked spending — will determine which platforms survive the current quick commerce boom.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC Bars Tech YouTubers TechWiser and TechBar From Criticising AI+ Smartphones Without Hearing
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court has issued an ex-parte order restraining technology content creators TechWiser and TechBar from making disparaging statements about a brand called AI+ Smartphones, without giving the creators an opportunity to be heard before the order was passed. The case raises urgent questions about the use of interim court orders to silence critical online speech about consumer technology products in India. Legal observers warn that such ex-parte restraints on content creators set a troubling precedent for free expression in digital product journalism.

video:video.video:title: Chiratae Ventures Commits $10M to Five Indian Deeptech Startups in Single Deployment
video:video.video:description: Chiratae Ventures has committed $10 million across five deeptech startups in India as part of a targeted bet on the country's untapped advanced technology potential. The fund sees deeptech — spanning areas like AI, semiconductors, and frontier science — as an emerging breakout category in India's startup ecosystem. The names of the five startups have not yet been disclosed publicly.

video:video.video:title: Paytm Posts First-Ever Annual Profit of Rs 552 Crore in FY26 After Years of Losses
video:video.video:description: Digital payments leader Paytm has recorded its first-ever full-year net profit of Rs 552 crore in FY26, swinging from significant losses in prior years. The turnaround was driven by disciplined cost control and a 22% rise in operating revenue to Rs 8,437 crore, with financial services emerging as the primary growth engine. The milestone is significant for India's fintech sector, signalling that large-scale digital payments platforms can achieve sustainable profitability after extended investment phases.

video:video.video:title: DesignX Builds Factory OS and Vish.ai to Turn Industrial Data Into Real-Time Decisions for 30+ Enter
video:video.video:description: Indian startup DesignX has developed Df-OS, a factory operating system, and Vish.ai, an AI decision layer, that convert raw factory data into actionable operational decisions in real time. The platform is already deployed across more than 30 enterprises including Unilever, Hero, and ITC, positioning DesignX as a meaningful player in India's industrial AI space. The solution targets manufacturing efficiency bottlenecks by replacing manual data interpretation with autonomous AI-driven recommendations.

video:video.video:title: Coforge CEO: AI Is Changing Tech Services Demand, Not Killing It — Firms That Lead Outcomes Will Win
video:video.video:description: Coforge CEO Sudhir Singh has publicly pushed back against narratives of AI-led demand collapse in IT services, arguing that the market is evolving into new value pools centred on AI-led modernisation and governance. He dismissed fears of AI firms displacing traditional IT services companies, framing them as specialists within a broader, growing market. The statement carries weight given Coforge's Q4 FY26 profit more than doubled to Rs 612 crore, suggesting its own AI-driven approach is yielding results.

video:video.video:title: Meesho Says 70% of Its Code Is Now AI-Written as Revenue Jumps 47% to Rs 3,531 Crore in Q4
video:video.video:description: Indian e-commerce platform Meesho has disclosed that over 70% of its codebase is now generated using artificial intelligence, with more than three-quarters of its orders driven by an AI recommendation engine. The company posted a 47% revenue jump to Rs 3,531 crore in Q4 FY26, narrowing its net loss by 88% year-on-year to Rs 166 crore. CEO Vidit Aatrey framed AI not just as a productivity tool but as a core commercial engine powering Meesho's path to profitability.

video:video.video:title: GoKwik Launches AI-Powered Kwik Ship to Cut Failed E-Commerce Deliveries by 20% Across India
video:video.video:description: GoKwik has launched Kwik Ship, an AI-powered logistics platform designed to reduce failed deliveries by up to 20% for Indian e-commerce brands. The system uses AI-powered calls and automated WhatsApp notifications to keep customers informed and provides more accurate delivery time estimates at checkout. The platform directly addresses one of Indian e-commerce's most persistent pain points — high return-to-origin rates caused by failed deliveries.

video:video.video:title: Bajaj Finance Cuts FY27 Autonomous AI Agent Target From 800 to 600 After Sales Scope Reduction
video:video.video:description: Bajaj Finance has revised its ambitious autonomous AI agent deployment target for FY27 downward from 800-plus to 600, after dropping the sales-related scope of the programme. As of Q4 FY26, only 27 agents are live with 118 more in planning, indicating deployment is running significantly behind the original schedule. The revision highlights the gap between enterprise AI ambitions and the operational realities of deploying autonomous agents at scale in India's financial services sector.

video:video.video:title: Skyroot Aerospace Raises $60M, Becomes India's First Spacetech Unicorn Ahead of Vikram-1 Launch
video:video.video:description: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace has raised $60 million in fresh funding, becoming India's first spacetech unicorn at a valuation crossing $1 billion. The capital will be used to support commercial launch operations of the Vikram-1 rocket, which is preparing for its inaugural orbital flight from Sriharikota. The milestone signals a maturing private space sector in India backed by policy reform and investor confidence.

video:video.video:title: Paytm Bets on Agentic AI and Wealthtech as Core Growth Pillars After RBI Payments Bank Shutdown
video:video.video:description: In its Q4 FY26 earnings call, Paytm revealed a strategic pivot toward agentic AI and wealthtech services as the primary drivers of its next growth phase, following the RBI-mandated shutdown of its payments bank arm. The company has ruled out applying for an NBFC licence, instead focusing on AI-powered financial tools and investment products for its existing user base. The shift represents a significant repositioning of one of India's largest fintech platforms toward autonomous AI-driven financial services.

video:video.video:title: Freshworks Cuts 11% of Workforce as AI Reshapes Indian-Founded Software Sector
video:video.video:description: Freshworks, the Indian-founded SaaS giant now headquartered in the US, has announced it will cut approximately 11% of its global workforce as AI tools increasingly automate tasks previously handled by human employees. The company cited the rapid adoption of AI-driven software development and support tools as a structural driver of the restructuring. The cuts signal a broader pattern in the Indian-origin tech industry where AI productivity gains are directly translating into workforce reductions.

video:video.video:title: Supreme Court Asks Bar Council to Form AI Expert Panel After Trial Court Cites Fake Judgments
video:video.video:description: India's Supreme Court has intervened after fake AI-generated judgments were cited in a lower court case, directing the Bar Council of India to constitute an expert panel on AI use in the judiciary. The development marks a landmark moment for how AI tools are regulated within India's legal system. The outcome of this panel could set binding guidelines for lawyers and judges across the country on the permissible use of AI research tools.

video:video.video:title: SEBI Orders Immediate Cybersecurity Overhaul Across All Regulated Entities, Citing Claude Mythos Ris
video:video.video:description: India's Securities and Exchange Board of India has issued a formal cybersecurity circular naming Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI system as a specific threat, ordering every regulated financial entity to urgently strengthen its cyber defences. SEBI has also formed a dedicated task force to oversee the overhaul. This is the first time SEBI has named a specific AI capability in a regulatory circular, marking a significant escalation in how Indian financial regulators treat advanced AI as a systemic risk.

video:video.video:title: Delhi HC Orders Removal of Deepfake Videos Falsely Showing MP Shashi Tharoor Praising Pakistan
video:video.video:description: The Delhi High Court announced it would issue blocking orders against AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting Congress MP Shashi Tharoor praising Pakistan, after he filed a petition over the misuse of his identity. The case marks one of the most prominent Indian legal interventions involving political deepfakes during an active security-sensitive period. The ruling signals growing judicial willingness to act swiftly against AI-generated political disinformation in India.

video:video.video:title: Digi Yatra Develops AI-Powered E-Passport Enrolment and Facial Verification System for International
video:video.video:description: Digi Yatra Foundation has shared new details of its proposed international travel system, which includes e-passport enrolment, AI-based facial verification, and token-based identity sharing to streamline border crossings for Indian travellers. The system builds on Digi Yatra's existing domestic airport face-recognition infrastructure, extending its ambition from domestic terminals to cross-border identity management. Privacy advocates are monitoring how biometric tokens will be stored, shared, and deleted across jurisdictions.

video:video.video:title: India Cabinet Approves Two Gujarat Semiconductor Units Worth Rs 3,936 Crore, Creating 2,230 Jobs
video:video.video:description: India's Union Cabinet has approved two new semiconductor manufacturing units in Gujarat with a combined investment of approximately Rs 3,936 crore, expected to generate around 2,230 skilled jobs. The approval is part of the government's ongoing push to build domestic chip manufacturing capacity as demand from AI, automotive, and consumer electronics sectors accelerates. The projects deepen India's semiconductor ecosystem beyond assembly and testing into more capital-intensive fabrication segments.

video:video.video:title: Fake Allu Arjun AI Chatbots Remain Live on CelebsGPT Despite Delhi High Court Personality Rights Ord
video:video.video:description: AI platform CelebsGPT continues to host fake chatbots mimicking actor Allu Arjun despite a Delhi High Court order granting him personality rights protection. The bots are styled as celebrity-character AI avatars and remain accessible on both the CelebsGPT site and Instagram, exposing a significant enforcement gap in India's emerging AI personality-rights jurisprudence. The case highlights the difficulty courts face in compelling removal of AI-generated impersonations from platforms with limited Indian regulatory reach.

video:video.video:title: Premji Invest in Talks to Join Emergent's $250M Fundraise at $1.5 Billion Valuation
video:video.video:description: Premji Invest is reportedly in advanced discussions to participate in AI coding platform Emergent's $250 million funding round, which would value the company at $1.5 billion. This follows Emergent's $70 million raise just three months earlier, signalling rapid investor confidence in AI-native software development tools. The potential backing from one of India's most respected institutional investors would further validate Emergent's position in the fast-growing agentic coding space.

video:video.video:title: Coforge Q4 FY26 Profit More Than Doubles to Rs 612 Crore, Driven by AI Efficiencies and Deal Wins
video:video.video:description: Coforge reported a 135% year-on-year surge in net profit to Rs 612 crore for Q4 FY26, surpassing street estimates, with strong revenue growth across healthcare and hi-tech verticals. The IT services firm attributed gains to AI-driven efficiencies and a robust pipeline of new deal wins. The result stands in contrast to the tepid growth reported by India's largest IT firms, suggesting mid-tier players are capturing AI-era benefits faster.

video:video.video:title: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Enterprise Tool — Falls Short of Mythos-Level Capabilities
video:video.video:description: Anthropic has launched Claude Security, an AI-powered vulnerability scanner built on its Opus 4.7 model, aimed at enterprise customers seeking automated cybersecurity tools. The product was released weeks after the Mythos zero-day threat triggered global alarm, but Anthropic has confirmed it does not carry Mythos-level offensive capabilities. Indian enterprises and CERT-In had been assessing exposure risks from Mythos, making this product launch directly relevant to India's cybersecurity posture.

video:video.video:title: Krutrim Pauses Chip Design and Foundation AI Model Work, Pivots Fully to AI Cloud Services
video:video.video:description: Krutrim, Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal's AI company, has paused its semiconductor chip design and foundation AI model programmes, redirecting capital and staff toward AI cloud services after a business realignment in late 2025. The pivot follows earlier reporting that Krutrim posted its first net profit in FY26 on the back of 3x revenue growth from cloud services. The strategic retreat from chip and model development narrows India's ambition for a fully indigenous AI stack but reflects capital discipline amid intense global competition.

video:video.video:title: Pixxel and Sarvam AI to Launch India's First Orbital AI Data Centre Satellite in 2026
video:video.video:description: Pixxel will design, build, launch, and operate India's first orbital data centre satellite, while Sarvam AI will run AI training and inference directly on board the spacecraft, eliminating dependence on cloud or ground infrastructure. Sarvam says the approach will reduce latency by cutting the round-trip time for data to reach the ground, enabling faster AI outputs from space-based systems. The collaboration represents a convergence of India's private space and sovereign AI ambitions in a single mission.

video:video.video:title: Pixxel Wins US National Reconnaissance Office Contract to Supply Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel has secured a contract from the US National Reconnaissance Office to provide hyperspectral satellite imagery, marking a significant commercial validation for an Indian private space firm. The award supports Washington's effort to integrate emerging commercial hyperspectral data sources into its expanding remote sensing architecture. It positions Pixxel as a credible supplier to one of the world's most demanding intelligence-grade customers.

video:video.video:title: Indian Cybersecurity Firms Deploy In-House AI Agents to Cut Vulnerability Response From Days to Hour
video:video.video:description: Indian cybersecurity companies are building proprietary AI agents on top of large language models to detect and remediate software vulnerabilities in hours rather than days. The shift is driven by attackers operating at machine speed, leaving human-only response cycles dangerously slow. Firms say the in-house approach gives them tighter control over sensitive client data compared to third-party tools.

video:video.video:title: FarMart Turns EBITDA Profitable in Q4 FY26, Hits Rs 3,600 Crore Run Rate With AI-Powered Agri Workfl
video:video.video:description: Agrifood platform FarMart has reached EBITDA profitability in Q4 FY26 and achieved a Rs 3,600 crore annualised revenue run rate, attributing its 50 percent year-on-year growth to deeper farmer wallet share, stronger supply chain networks, and AI-powered workflows across its operations. The decade-old platform connects farmers, input suppliers, and agri-businesses, with AI now embedded in procurement, logistics, and advisory services. The milestone is significant for India's agritech sector, which has seen multiple high-profile shutdowns in recent years.

video:video.video:title: Curium Life's SurgiMeasure Brings Real-Time AI Intelligence to Indian Operating Theatres
video:video.video:description: Curium Life, an Indian healthtech startup, has developed SurgiMeasure, an AI-powered surgical intelligence tool that delivers real-time intraoperative insights to surgeons during procedures. The platform is backed by clinical studies and has attracted global collaborators, positioning India as an emerging hub for surgical AI innovation. The tool aims to improve surgical precision and outcomes by giving operating theatre teams data-driven guidance at the moment of decision.

video:video.video:title: Perceptyne Builds AI-Powered Dual-Arm Robots for India's Factory Floors With Flexible Low-Cost Deplo
video:video.video:description: Indian startup Perceptyne is developing AI-driven dual-arm robotic systems designed to automate complex manufacturing tasks that traditional industrial robots cannot perform cost-effectively. The company positions its robots as flexible and affordable enough for mid-sized Indian factories, aiming to reduce the barrier to automation that has historically kept smaller manufacturers from deploying robotics. The startup enters a manufacturing sector where AI-driven automation is increasingly reshaping the nature of factory work across India.

video:video.video:title: Razorpay Gets Shareholder Approval for Rs 2,700 Crore IPO as Fintech Bets on AI Amid Rising Losses
video:video.video:description: Indian fintech giant Razorpay has secured shareholder approval to raise Rs 2,700 crore through an IPO, which will include an offer for sale component and a pre-IPO placement tranche. The company is positioning AI-driven payment infrastructure as a central growth narrative for its public market debut, even as it continues to report net losses amid intense competition in India's digital payments sector. A successful listing would be a major milestone for India's fintech ecosystem and would test public market appetite for loss-making AI-first fintech platforms.

video:video.video:title: Dream Sports Launches AI-Powered Stock Broking Platform DreamStreet to Target First-Time Indian Inve
video:video.video:description: Dream Sports, the parent company of fantasy sports platform Dream11, has launched DreamStreet, a new AI-powered stockbroking platform specifically designed to simplify equity investing for first-time retail investors in India. The platform uses AI to generate personalised investment insights and provides access to licensed research analysts to guide users who are new to financial markets. The move represents Dream Sports' diversification beyond gaming following regulatory changes that impacted its core fantasy sports business.

video:video.video:title: Digi Yatra Builds AI-Powered E-Passport Enrolment System for International Travel Using Facial Verif
video:video.video:description: The Digi Yatra Foundation has revealed new details of a proposed international travel system that combines e-passport enrolment, AI-powered facial verification, and token-based digital identity sharing at border checkpoints. The system aims to extend India's domestic airport biometric check-in infrastructure to cross-border travel, potentially affecting tens of millions of Indian passport holders. Privacy advocates have flagged concerns about data storage, biometric consent, and interoperability with foreign immigration systems.

video:video.video:title: Fake Allu Arjun AI Chatbots Remain Live Despite Delhi High Court Personality Rights Order
video:video.video:description: AI platform CelebsGPT continues to host unauthorised chatbots mimicking actor Allu Arjun's persona on its platform and via Instagram, despite the Delhi High Court having granted him personality rights protection in an ongoing case. The persistence of these fake AI avatars after a court order highlights a growing enforcement gap in India's nascent AI personality rights framework. Legal experts say the case tests whether Indian courts can compel AI platforms — many of which are foreign-operated — to comply with domestic personality rights rulings.

video:video.video:title: Yotta Data Hires Advisors for $900 Million India IPO, Targeting $6 Billion Valuation on AI Demand
video:video.video:description: Yotta Data Services, a key player in India's AI infrastructure build-out, is planning a Mumbai IPO to raise up to $900 million and is also considering a $300 million pre-IPO placement round. The company is targeting a valuation of approximately $6 billion, buoyed by surging demand for data centre capacity driven by AI workloads across India. This IPO, if completed, would be one of the largest technology listings in India in recent years and signals strong investor conviction in the country's AI infrastructure story.

video:video.video:title: Pixxel and Sarvam AI to Launch India's First Orbital Data Centre Satellite in 2026
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based space tech startup Pixxel is set to launch India's first orbital data centre satellite this year, with Sarvam AI providing the onboard AI backbone for the mission. Pixxel will design, build, launch, and operate the satellite, marking a convergence of India's fast-growing space and AI sectors. The collaboration positions India as one of very few countries attempting to place AI computing capability directly in orbit.

video:video.video:title: Krutrim Pivots to AI Cloud Services, Reports 3x Revenue Growth and First Net Profit in FY26
video:video.video:description: Krutrim, India's first AI unicorn, has announced a strategic pivot to become a focused domestic AI Cloud Services provider, reporting its first annual net profit in FY26 alongside threefold revenue growth. The company's platform is built entirely in-house and now serves over 25 large enterprise customers across multiple sectors. This marks a significant shift from a broad AI model developer to a sustainable, infrastructure-led cloud business — a milestone for India's homegrown AI industry.

video:video.video:title: ISB DLabs I-HEAL Fourth Cohort: 15 Health Startups Building AI-Led Solutions for India's Most Overlo
video:video.video:description: The Indian School of Business's DLabs accelerator has unveiled 15 startups in the fourth cohort of its I-HEAL healthcare programme, each targeting persistent and underserved gaps across India's health system — from diagnostics and rehabilitation to hearing health, which affects over 63 million Indians. The cohort reflects a broader push to build technology-enabled solutions that can reach patients beyond urban hospital infrastructure. Several startups are deploying AI for early diagnosis, remote monitoring, and personalised care pathways in areas where specialist access is limited. The programme positions ISB as a key institutional bridge between academic research and applied health innovation in India.

video:video.video:title: MeitY's Section 69A Blocked Anti-Gambling App Gamban for Three Years Without Disclosing Reasons
video:video.video:description: UK-based Gamban, an app designed to help people block access to gambling sites and protect themselves from addiction, says India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology blocked it under Section 69A of the IT Act for three years without providing any reasons or formal order. MeitY has cited privacy concerns as a justification, but Gamban's representatives describe the block as arbitrary and legally unfounded, noting the irony of a harm-reduction tool being censored without explanation. The case spotlights how opaque India's content blocking regime can be, even when the affected party is a consumer protection service. It adds a concrete new example to ongoing debates about the accountability and proportionality of Section 69A orders.

video:video.video:title: Skyroot's Vikram-1 — India's First Private Orbital Rocket — Set for Launch From Sriharikota Within W
video:video.video:description: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace is weeks away from launching Vikram-1, which would become India's first privately developed orbital rocket to reach space, lifting off from ISRO's Sriharikota launch facility. The test flight will carry diverse payloads and is designed primarily to gather engineering data that will underpin future commercial missions. A successful launch would establish Skyroot as a credible competitor for global satellite launch contracts, building on India's reputation as a cost-effective launch destination. The milestone reflects the maturation of India's private space sector following policy reforms that opened ISRO's infrastructure to commercial operators.

video:video.video:title: Independent Media and Online Critics Face Growing Censorship Risk as India's Content Takedown Infras
video:video.video:description: An investigative report by The Hindu finds that an expanding infrastructure of content takedown mechanisms — enabled by existing laws and IT rules — is being used by Central and State governments to suppress social media content, with independent media outlets and online critics increasingly caught in its crosshairs. The report documents how, in an environment of heightened concern about misinformation and deepfakes, legitimate opposing voices are also being targeted under the same regulatory tools. The analysis highlights how the lack of transparency in takedown orders makes it nearly impossible for affected parties to challenge removals. The piece adds fresh evidence to ongoing expert concerns about the erosion of digital free speech in India.

video:video.video:title: Apple Calls India's Competition Commission an Overreach as CCI-Apple Antitrust Dispute Intensifies
video:video.video:description: Apple has formally accused India's Competition Commission (CCI) of overstepping its judicial authority after the regulator sought detailed financial information from the company — data typically requested when calculating penalties — following a 2024 investigation that found Apple abused its dominant position in the Indian app marketplace. Apple has disputed the CCI's jurisdiction to compel such disclosures, escalating what began as a regulatory inquiry into a high-stakes legal confrontation. The dispute has significant implications for how India regulates Big Tech, particularly as the government attempts to assert stronger sovereign oversight over dominant platform ecosystems. The outcome could set a precedent for how foreign tech giants respond to Indian antitrust authority.

video:video.video:title: IndiaMART Stops Reporting Traffic Metrics as AI Agent Bots Overwhelm Platform With Agentic Traffic
video:video.video:description: IndiaMART, India's largest B2B e-commerce marketplace, has quietly stopped disclosing its 'unique business inquiries' traffic metric after agentic AI bots began flooding the platform with automated queries, distorting data that investors and sellers had relied on to gauge platform health. The company introduced OTP verification to filter bot traffic, but this created a 1% drop in genuine user conversion in Q4 FY26, illustrating the trade-off between data integrity and user friction. The shift marks a significant moment for Indian digital commerce: AI agents are now active enough to meaningfully disrupt the reporting and operations of a major public platform. This is one of the first documented cases of an Indian company formally abandoning a key business metric due to AI agent interference.

video:video.video:title: Tata Electronics Targets $30 Billion Revenue With India's First Semiconductor Fab and Global Custome
video:video.video:description: Tata Electronics CEO and MD Randhir Thakur says the company aims to become a $30 billion business within five years, anchored by India's first semiconductor fabrication plant and an assembly and test unit currently under construction. The company has already achieved significant revenue growth and crossed into profitability, while securing global customers and manufacturing partnerships. Tata Electronics is simultaneously scaling its iPhone component manufacturing operations, making it one of India's most strategically significant industrial plays in electronics and semiconductors. The ambition positions India as a genuine alternative to China in global chip supply chains.

video:video.video:title: UpGrad to Acquire Unacademy for Rs 2,055 Crore — 90% Below Peak Valuation in India's Edtech Reckonin
video:video.video:description: Ronnie Screwvala's UpGrad is set to acquire Unacademy for approximately Rs 2,055 crore — a valuation nearly 90% below Unacademy's peak of over Rs 20,000 crore — marking one of the starkest corrections in India's edtech sector since its pandemic-era peak. The deal, which follows months of on-again, off-again negotiations, is being financed partly through an internal fundraising round of approximately Rs 375 crore from existing backers including Temasek, a common investor in both companies. The consolidation reflects broader pressure on India's online learning platforms as post-COVID enrolment normalised and profitability proved elusive. The combined entity would position UpGrad as India's dominant working-professional upskilling platform.

video:video.video:title: India's Major IT Firms Record Rising Revenue Per Employee as AI and Automation Drive Productivity Sh
video:video.video:description: India's top IT companies — including TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra — have reported measurable increases in revenue generated per employee, a metric that signals a structural shift away from the traditional headcount-driven business model. Analysts attribute the gains to widespread adoption of AI coding assistants, automation of routine service tasks, and leaner project delivery pipelines. The trend suggests firms are extracting more value from existing workforces rather than scaling headcount proportionally with revenue. This marks one of the clearest financial confirmations yet that AI-led productivity is reshaping how India's $250-billion IT industry operates.

video:video.video:title: GalaxEye Launches World's First OptoSAR Satellite — India's Largest Private Space Payload Reaches Or
video:video.video:description: Indian deep-tech startup GalaxEye successfully launched Mission Drishti aboard a SpaceX rocket, making it the world's first satellite to combine electro-optical and synthetic aperture radar (OptoSAR) sensors in a single 190-kilogram platform — the largest satellite ever built by an Indian private company. The satellite is designed to capture high-quality Earth observation data regardless of weather or lighting conditions, overcoming limitations of conventional single-sensor systems. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly hailed the launch as a landmark achievement for India's private space sector. GalaxEye expects to begin commercial data sales within eight weeks, with defence and security agencies anticipated as anchor customers.

video:video.video:title: MobiKwik Secures NBFC Licence From RBI, Launches Own Lending Subsidiary to Move Beyond Distribution
video:video.video:description: Digital payments and financial services platform MobiKwik has received a Non-Banking Financial Company licence from the Reserve Bank of India, allowing it to launch its own lending subsidiary, MobiKwik Financial Services Private Limited, and move from being a lending distributor to a direct lender. The NBFC licence is a significant regulatory milestone that gives MobiKwik control over its own credit products, pricing, and underwriting rather than acting as a pass-through for partner NBFCs. This transition is expected to improve unit economics and enable the platform to offer more competitive loan products to its user base of tens of millions of Indians.

video:video.video:title: Snabbit Raises $56M in Six Months After Last Round as Instant Home Services Race Intensifies in Indi
video:video.video:description: On-demand home services startup Snabbit has raised $56 million in a new round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann India Investments, bringing its total capital raised to $112 million in under a year. The rapid successive fundraising reflects intensifying investor interest in India's instant home services category, where Snabbit competes to connect urban households with vetted domestic help on short notice. The company plans to use the capital to expand city coverage and deepen its service category range.

video:video.video:title: HyugaLife Raises Rs 100 Crore Series A to Scale AI Personalisation and Dark Store Network Across Ind
video:video.video:description: Health and wellness e-commerce platform HyugaLife has closed a Rs 100 crore Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures, which it will deploy to strengthen its AI-driven personalisation engine, expand its dark store fulfilment network, and open offline retail touchpoints. The company uses AI to match customers with personalised health product recommendations based on lifestyle data, aiming to compete in India's rapidly growing wellness commerce segment. The funding positions HyugaLife to scale beyond its current urban customer base into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

video:video.video:title: Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech Form Rs 100-Crore JV With Israel's Xtend to Make Drones in India
video:video.video:description: Indian technology firms Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech have announced a Rs 100-crore joint venture with Israeli drone technology company Xtend to manufacture advanced unmanned aerial vehicles in India. The JV aims to meet India's growing demand for sophisticated drones, with the first production-ready drone sets expected within four to six months. The initiative aligns with India's Make in India push for defence and dual-use technology self-reliance, reducing dependence on imported UAV systems.

video:video.video:title: Sahamati Raises Rs 50 Crore to Deepen India's Account Aggregator Ecosystem
video:video.video:description: Sahamati, the industry alliance backing India's Account Aggregator financial data-sharing framework, has raised Rs 50 crore from financial sector entities to strengthen its technical and policy infrastructure. The capital will be used to deepen ecosystem participation among banks, insurers, and fintech players who use the AA framework to enable consent-based financial data sharing for millions of Indians. The Account Aggregator system is a foundational piece of India's Digital Public Infrastructure and underpins credit access for underserved borrowers.

video:video.video:title: Paytring Uses OpenAI Models to Fix Payment Chaos for Indian Merchants — Founder Explains How
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Paytring has built a payment orchestration layer for Indian merchants that uses OpenAI's language models to improve transaction success rates and simplify checkout operations. Founder Debal Chakraborty explains that AI is used to route payments intelligently across multiple gateways, reducing failures that cost merchants revenue on every failed transaction. The startup addresses a gap in India's booming digital payments ecosystem where checkout friction remains a persistent problem for small and mid-sized businesses.

video:video.video:title: India's Content Takedown Rules Under Scrutiny: Experts Warn of Expanding Powers With No Transparency
video:video.video:description: A MediaNama discussion surfaced expert warnings that India's content-blocking legal framework is being expanded through draft IT Rules in ways that are largely hidden from public view, with experts saying what is not disclosed may be more consequential than what is. Former MeitY official Rakesh Maheshwari and former Meta public policy manager Snehashish Ghosh traced the origins of the three-hour content takedown mandate to the 2019 election code of ethics, revealing how an emergency electoral measure has been normalised into permanent regulatory architecture. Panellists warned that the lack of transparency in how blocking decisions are made leaves citizens and platforms with no meaningful redress.

video:video.video:title: India's Draft IT Rules Trigger Free Speech Fears as IDC Gains Powers to Block Online Content
video:video.video:description: The Hindu's editorial analysis of India's proposed IT Rules amendments warns that the draft departs from existing Supreme Court rulings and consolidates content-blocking authority in the executive, raising the risk of digital overreach. The piece highlights how the proposed Inter-Departmental Committee structure lacks judicial checks, giving bureaucrats power to restrict online speech without transparency or appeal mechanisms. Legal experts cited in the article argue the rules conflict with constitutional free speech protections.

video:video.video:title: Experts Warn MeitY's Draft IT Rules Give Executive Power to Issue Binding AI Advisories, Bypassing P
video:video.video:description: Legal and policy experts at a MediaNama event raised serious alarms over proposed Rule 3(4) in India's draft IT Rules amendments, which they say allows MeitY to issue binding advisories, guidelines, and standard operating procedures without parliamentary oversight or judicial review. Critics argue the provision effectively hands the executive branch unchecked authority to shape what speech is permissible online, with no mandatory transparency mechanism. The concern is compounded by separate warnings about an Inter-Departmental Committee being granted expansive powers to act as 'judge, jury, and executioner' over online content.

video:video.video:title: MeitY Secretary Confirms India in Direct Talks With Anthropic Over Mythos Cybersecurity Threat
video:video.video:description: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed the Union government is in direct talks with Anthropic regarding concerns over the Mythos AI model, describing AI's impact on cybersecurity as a 'very real threat' that has materialised 'in very real terms.' The development signals the Indian government's escalating concern about advanced AI capabilities posing risks to national digital infrastructure. This is the first confirmed high-level bilateral engagement between MeitY and Anthropic specifically on the Mythos vulnerability.

video:video.video:title: Infosys Delays Salary Hike Decision Amid AI-Driven Cost Pressures and Cautious FY27 Revenue Outlook
video:video.video:description: Infosys management has told employees at a recent town hall that the company has not yet decided on salary revision timelines, citing macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious client spending — with communication already delayed by four months. The non-commitment comes as Infosys forecasts modest revenue growth for FY27 and faces compounding pressure from AI-driven productivity tools that are reducing billable headcount requirements. The development signals broader structural tension across India's IT sector, where AI efficiency gains are increasingly being absorbed as margin improvement rather than passed on to employees as wage growth.

video:video.video:title: IAMAI Alleges TRAI Is Overstepping to Regulate OTT Platforms Like WhatsApp Under Spam Call Rules
video:video.video:description: India's Internet and Mobile Association (IAMAI) has formally alleged that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is exceeding its jurisdiction by attempting to bring over-the-top platforms such as WhatsApp under the scope of proposed anti-spam regulations designed for traditional telecom services. IAMAI argues that OTT platforms are not telecommunications services and that requiring them to share user data under these rules would be unconstitutional. The dispute raises fundamental questions about regulatory boundaries in an era where AI-driven communication platforms increasingly blur the line between telecom and internet services.

video:video.video:title: Jamtara Is Old News: How AI-Powered Synthetic Identity Fraud Is Now Threatening India's Digital Lend
video:video.video:description: As India's digital lending sector scales rapidly, AI-powered synthetic identity fraud has emerged as a structural threat to the underwriting models that lenders rely upon, according to a YourStory analysis. Fraudsters are now using generative AI to construct convincing fake identities — combining real and fabricated personal data — that pass conventional KYC and credit scoring checks, forcing lenders to rethink risk assessment from the ground up. The piece argues that fraud is no longer a downstream compliance problem but has become an upstream design challenge embedded in how digital credit is originated in India.

video:video.video:title: Infosys Co-Founder Kris Gopalakrishnan: Deep Tech and Advanced Manufacturing Will Drive India's Unic
video:video.video:description: Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan has called for India's next generation of startups to anchor themselves in deep technology and advanced manufacturing rather than software services, framing this pivot as essential for national self-reliance and long-term competitive advantage. Gopalakrishnan described this shift as 'Unicorn 2.0', arguing that proprietary technology — including AI — must underpin future high-value companies rather than imported platforms or service arbitrage. His remarks carry weight given Infosys's own AI-driven restructuring pressures and reflect a growing consensus among India's senior tech leadership about where sustainable value creation lies.

video:video.video:title: NITI Aayog Report: India's Digital Public Infrastructure Could Contribute 4% of GDP by 2030
video:video.video:description: A new NITI Aayog report titled 'DPI@2047 for Viksit Bharat' projects that India's Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives — including UPI, Aadhaar, and emerging AI-linked data layers — could contribute up to 4% of GDP by 2030, describing the current moment as a 'once-in-a-generation inflection point'.
